closed.name: MyForexFunds
closed.status_reason: Operations stopped on 29 Aug 2023 when a US court froze assets on the CFTC's application and the Ontario Securities Commission issued a temporary cease-trade order. The CFTC case was later dismissed with prejudice as a sanction against the CFTC (order of 13 May 2025); no court made a finding of fraud. The brand has not sold challenges since, and its website announces a relaunch on 23 Nov 2026.
closed.what_happened: On 29 Aug 2023 the CFTC filed a complaint in the US District Court for the District of New Jersey (Case 1:23-cv-11808) against Traders Global Group Inc. and Murtuza Kazmi, alleging they fraudulently solicited customers. The same day it got an ex parte statutory restraining order that froze assets and appointed a temporary receiver. Also on 29 Aug 2023, the OSC issued a temporary cease-trade order. Tribunal extensions followed, the last on 18 Jul 2024 (consented to by the respondents), and that order expired after at most 3 months. The tribunal docket lists no later filings. Grant Thornton Limited was appointed receiver and manager by the Ontario Superior Court of Justice on 21 Dec 2023. In Nov 2023 the US court narrowed the freeze and removed the temporary receiver. On 13 May 2025, Judge Edward S. Kiel adopted the Special Master's report, granted the defendants' Rule 11 sanctions motion and dismissed the complaint with prejudice. On 11 Jul 2025 the court awarded the defendants $3,148,484.22 in legal fees and costs from the CFTC and closed the case. In April 2026, FNG reported that MFF had begun returning funds to clients who had pending rewards. The brand has since been sold to Global Solutions Operations FZE (Dubai), which says it is 'not currently offering any products or services under the MyForexFunds brand' and has announced a relaunch on 23 Nov 2026.

regulator.name: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC); Ontario Securities Commission (OSC)
regulator.action: CFTC civil complaint and statutory restraining order (D.N.J., filed 29 Aug 2023), dismissed with prejudice on 13 May 2025 as a Rule 11 sanction against the CFTC. OSC temporary cease-trade order of 29 Aug 2023, last extended 18 Jul 2024 for up to 3 months; no statement of allegations appears on the Capital Markets Tribunal docket.
regulator.quote: The Sanction Motion (ECF No. 172) is GRANTED and the complaint is dismissed with prejudice.

closed.trader_action: MyForexFunds says traders with accounts active before 29 Aug 2023 should use its claims and restoration process, which Global Solutions Operations FZE now runs on Traders Global's behalf (https://myforexfunds.com/myforexfunds-returns/ and https://myforexfunds.com/myforexfunds-announces-new-ownership/). The firm describes this as a discretionary program, not a court-ordered one.

closed.name: Seacrest Funded
closed.status_reason: According to Finance Magnates (4 Feb 2026), Seacrest Markets closed its prop-trading operations, with all prop accounts and open positions closed on 6 Feb 2026, to focus on its CFD brokerage. Seacrest Markets' own website now says it 'is no longer operating'.
closed.what_happened: In Feb 2025, MyFundedFX, a Dallas, Texas group, rebranded as SeacrestFunded under its South African FSCA-licensed broker Seacrest Markets and stopped onboarding US clients. On 4 Feb 2026, Seacrest announced it would end prop trading. All prop accounts and positions were closed on 6 Feb 2026. Active, unbreached challenge holders could request refunds, and funded traders their final payouts, by 28 Feb 2026. At the time, Finance Magnates said futures prop trading continued under MyFunded Futures. Today myfundedfx.com redirects to seacrestmarkets.io/closed, which says Seacrest Markets is no longer operating, and seacrestfunded.com is a 'domain may be for sale' page.
closed.trader_action: The refund and final-payout window set by Seacrest closed on 28 Feb 2026, per Finance Magnates. The closure page gives support@seacrestmarkets.io for questions.
closed.hq: Dallas, Texas, USA (MyFundedFX); broker entity Seacrest Markets (PTY) Ltd, South Africa

closed.name: Traders With Edge
closed.status_reason: We found no closure announcement from the firm. Its domain no longer resolves, Trustpilot says the company's website has closed, and trade sites reported in Dec 2025 that the site had gone offline 'suggesting firm shutdown'.
closed.what_happened: Trustpilot reviews from Jul–Sep 2025 include customer allegations of denied payouts and of the platform being offline for weeks. These are allegations, not findings. On 29 Dec 2025, VettedPropFirms reported that the website had gone offline several days earlier with no public statement from the company. On 7 Sep 2026, BestForex.io reported that the domain does not resolve and that Trustpilot marks the website closed. On 31 Oct 2026, traderswithedge.com returned DNS 'name not resolved'.
closed.trader_action: BestForex.io suggests former customers keep invoices, agreements, account statements and support emails for any payment-provider or legal claim. That is general guidance, not a formal claims process.

closed.name: Propel Capital
closed.status_reason: On 19 Aug 2025, CEO Mitchell Ali posted on X that he had decided 'to wind down Propel Capital as you know it'. He cited heavy competition and said the firm would 'remove ourselves from the market with immediate effect', according to FX News Group.
closed.what_happened: Propel Capital, a London firm, was founded about 14 months before closing. On 19 Aug 2025 it stopped processing payments and halted all trading activity. It said it would wait a few weeks to see whether anyone wanted to continue the brand and then offer refunds to those who qualify. FNG reported that the website was down that day. On 31 Oct 2026 the domain showed only a 'verify you're human' gate, and the site certificate failed validation in a direct fetch.
closed.trader_action: In its statement, Propel said refunds would be offered 'to those who qualify', with updates via Discord, X and email, per FX News Group.

closed.name: FundingTicks
closed.status_reason: FundingTicks' website says 'as a strategic decision, we are winding down FundingTicks' operations'. Finance Magnates reported the wind-down on 19 Jan 2026, after a backlash over retroactive rule changes in Dec 2025.
closed.what_happened: In Dec 2025 the futures prop firm introduced new rules, including a one-minute minimum hold and reduced profit splits. Traders reported invalidated profits, and Trustpilot ratings fell. On 18 Jan 2026 it announced a full wind-down. Active Evals and Master accounts are refunded in full. Master accounts get an 80% or 20% reward split depending on whether objectives were met, and live accounts get refunds plus specified percentages. Support remained available until 31 Jan 2026. The wind-down notice is still the homepage.
closed.trader_action: According to FundingTicks and Finance Magnates, refunds and account handling were already under way and traders should check their dashboards. Support was available until 31 Jan 2026.

closed.name: Vault Funder
closed.status_reason: The firm's own page says 'Vault Funder is permanently closed' and 'The service will not reopen'. The page gives no closure date.
closed.what_happened: The closure page says challenges, funded accounts, competitions and affiliate programmes have all ended and that no registrations, purchases or payments are accepted. Active challenges, evaluations and funded accounts are being refunded in full, and earned unwithdrawn profit is being paid. Claims go only through an emailed claim form, and the firm warns of scammers asking for fees. It operated under the Vault Markets broker site. MyPropGenius first recorded the notice on 6 Oct 2026, and the exact closure date is unknown.
closed.trader_action: According to Vault Funder, clients with active accounts were emailed a claim form, the only accepted claims channel. Those who did not receive it should email the support address on https://vaultmarkets.trade/vaultfunder/ from their registered email with their account number. There is no fee to claim.
